newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria power company gets tough with debtors.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria power company gets tough with debtors.

text.p: Bulgaria's National Electricity Company (NEC) said on Monday it would curb supplies to some of its industrial clients who had not paid their bills.
A company statement said that unless customers paid up, the NEC, which supplies some 90 percent of Bulgaria's electricity, would not be able to keep its national grid functioning.

Debtors, mainly from the industrial sector, now owe the company more than 61 billion levs ($40.6 million). The debt to the NEC was some 40 billion levs at the end of April when the state supplier issued its last threat to cut off consumers.
Among 22 plants and water suppliers listed as not having paid their bills are a weapons producer in the town of Sopot, a pharmaceuticals plant in Razgrad and a paper plant in Belovo.
The company will completely cut electricity supplies unless debtors pay within five days.

The central bank barred commercial banks from lending to the NEC last year and the company, which owes some 40 billion levs to its suppliers, relies entirely on its income from selling electricity. $=1,500 levs
